title: Patch: the fuzz monitor checks that no unit token reaches a pile and that a position switch spends the exertion an attack needs

**Issue #2690 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2690: Patch: the fuzz monitor checks that no unit token reaches a pile and that a position switch spends the exertion an attack needs
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The random-game tester plays thousands of games through the engine and checks a list of rules after every move. Two rules the spec states plainly are not on that list: a unit token stops existing when it leaves the field, so it never lands in a graveyard or exile pile; and a unit gets one action a turn, an attack or a change of position, unless it has Deft. If the engine ever broke either, the tester would not notice. Once built, it checks both, so a bug that sends a token to the graveyard, or lets a unit switch and then attack, fails CI with its seed.

## Why
- §3 (`spec/03-zones.md:9`): Graveyard, “Unit tokens never enter it; spell tokens do.” §3.2 (`:34`): unit tokens cease to exist when they leave the field for any reason (R11).
- §4.1 (`spec/04-combat.md:8-9`): “Each unit has one exertion per turn: one attack or one position switch. A unit with Deft may do both (R49).”, and a Windfury unit's first attack spends the exertion a switch needs (R636).
- The monitor is `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`, I1–I10 (header `:46-150`). None scans a pile for unit tokens: `is_unit_token_def` (`:536`) is read only by I6's lineage. I2 counts only `attackDeclared` (`:2332` on) and I4(b) only `exertion.attacked`; nothing reads `exertion.switched`, `positionSwitched` or Deft. I8 cannot see a switch rule broken, since the listing and the reducer share one check (`crates/engine/src/combat.rs:178-191`, `:275-305`).
- R11 is kept by many separate paths, among them `zones.rs:594-597` (`is_unit_token`, which reads the type the card shows now, so a token set face-down reads as what it was set as), `effects/hold.rs:122`, `effects/transform.rs:130-135`, `effects/destroy.rs:129` and the sandbox's own graveyard push (`sandbox.rs:263-270`). Exertion is reset in several places too (`turn.rs:274-306`, `combat.rs:219-234`, the kill credit's fresh exertion in `effects/statuses.rs:81-106`).

## Proposal
- I11, after every action: no card whose definition is a unit token (`is_unit_token_def`, by definition, not by face) sits in either side's graveyard or exile, or in `state.held`.
- I12, beside I2's shadow: record a chosen `switchPosition` that emits `positionSwitched` per unit, keyed by turn and stint (`stint_of`); flag a switch or a declared attack in the same stint and turn that the unit's exertion did not allow, Deft read through the layers (`keywords_now`), Windfury's first attack spending the switch (R636), a kill credit's fresh exertion and a re-entry resetting it as I2 already treats them.
- Run both in the Duos per-duel monitor too, and plant a failing state for each in the monitor's tests, as #2568 did for I10.
- Run `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`, `--handicap` and `--duos`; a real violation found is fixed in the engine with its seed pinned, or split into its own issue if large.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` (header list and checks), `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` (its doc lines that list the checks)
- SPEC §3, §3.2, §4.1; R11, R49, R636

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A planted state with a unit token in a graveyard, in exile and in `held` each fails I11; a spell token in a graveyard passes.
- [ ] A planted non-Deft unit that switched and then declares an attack in the same stint fails I12; the same with Deft passes; a Windfury unit that attacked once and then switches fails.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`, `--handicap` and `--duos` pass, or each failure is fixed or filed with its seed.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, clippy and fmt pass.

## Size and risks
Medium: about 70 lines in the monitor and two planted tests. Risk: a first run may find false positives, as I6's did; each is fixed in the oracle with a comment naming the seed, and a real engine bug found is the point.

## Plan

_Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41325693791)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Extend the random-game invariant monitor with I11, which rejects definition-level Unit tokens in either graveyard, either exile pile, or `GameState::held`, while allowing Spell tokens in ordinary piles. Add I12 as an event-stream shadow of position-switch exertion so a non-Deft Unit cannot switch and declare an attack, or attack and then switch, in the same turn and field stint; preserve Deft, Windfury, re-entry, forced-attack, effect-switch, and confirmed kill-refresh semantics, including in Duos’ per-duel monitors.

## Files to touch

| Path | Status | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` | change | Document and implement I11/I12 in `InvariantMonitor`; keep `DuosInvariantMonitor` delegation current. |
| `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` | change | Add planted invalid-state/event tests for Unit-token piles and switch/attack exertion, with Spell-token and Deft controls. |
| `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` | change | Update the fuzz command’s invariant documentation from the old partial ranges to I1–I12 and name I11/I12. |
| `crates/tools/src/fused_pairs.rs` | change | Update the monitor range in the header because fused-pair games automatically run the same I1–I12 monitor. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | Update the fuzz and Duos command contract from I1–I10 to I1–I12, naming the two new always-on checks. |

Do not touch gameplay reducers such as `crates/engine/src/combat.rs`, state/wire surfaces, cards, the web app, generated files, or forbidden bot/workflow paths for the monitor-only implementation. Do not edit `spec/`: this adds no rules decision; it enforces existing SPEC §3 and §3.2/R11 plus §4.1/R49/R636.

## Steps

1. In `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`, change the module header from “ten checks” to “twelve checks” and add precise I11 and I12 paragraphs. State that I11 uses `is_unit_token_def`, not the card’s current face; that I12 counts only a chosen `ActionBody::SwitchPosition` confirmed by its matching `GameEvent::PositionSwitched`; that effect-driven switches and forced attacks spend nothing; and that Deft, Windfury, re-entry and a confirmed `mayAttackAgain` kill refresh follow R49/R636 and the existing stint/kill-credit shadow.

2. Beside `AttackMark`, add `SwitchMark { turn: i32, stint: i32 }` and `ChosenExertion { instance_id: String, def_id: String, kind: crate::combat::ExertionKind, deft: bool }`. Extend `InvariantMonitor` with `last_switch: IndexMap<String, SwitchMark>` and `chosen_exertion: Option<ChosenExertion>`. Initialize both in `InvariantMonitor::new`; at the start of every `before` call, replace `chosen_exertion` from the `Attack` or `SwitchPosition` Unit found in the pre-action state, using `keywords_now`/`has_keyword` for Deft, and set it to `None` for every other action.

3. Extend the event loop in `InvariantMonitor::after` for I12. On a non-forced `AttackDeclared`, resolve `instead_of` exactly as I2 does, then reject a `last_switch` with the same `turn` and `stint` unless the matching `ChosenExertion` says the attacker had layered Deft; do not count forced attacks. On `PositionSwitched`, record/check it only when it matches a `ChosenExertion` of `ExertionKind::Switch`, so R20 effect switches are ignored: reject a second switch in the same turn/stint even with Deft, and reject a switch after a declaration whose `AttackMark::count` is beyond `credited_at(id)` unless Deft applies. For an event not matching the chosen action, fall back to `find_instance` plus `keywords_now` only for its current layered Deft value. Emit deterministic messages beginning `I12`, naming the instance/definition and turn and citing §4.1, R49 and R636 as appropriate; consume `chosen_exertion` at the end of `after` so another Duos duel or later action cannot match it.

4. Integrate I12 with existing resets rather than reading `CardInstance::exertion` as the oracle. A call to `enter` already advances `stint`, so old switch/attack marks no longer match after re-entry. In `settle_kill_credits`, remove the old switch mark only in the branch where the settled state proves the kill really refreshed exertion (`attacked` is no longer spent); when the speculative credit is rolled back, retain the switch mark. Continue using `credited_at` as I2’s attack-count baseline, so a first Windfury attack still blocks switching but attacks before a confirmed fresh exertion do not.

5. Add `unit_token_pile_findings(state: &GameState) -> Vec<String>` and call it from the end of `InvariantMonitor::after` as I11’s always-on state scan. Walk both players in `PLAYER_IDS`, checking every graveyard and exile card, then `state.held.iter().flatten().map(|held| &held.card)`; for each card whose definition satisfies the existing `is_unit_token_def`, emit one `I11` finding with its id, definition, location and turn and cite §3, §3.2 and R11. Do not call `zones::is_unit_token`, because a face/layer change must not disguise the definition-level token. Update the `InvariantMonitor::after` and `DuosInvariantMonitor::after` comments to list I11/I12; the existing call to each duel’s `InvariantMonitor::after` must remain the single Duos integration path.

6. In `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs`, add `invariant(id: &str, found: Vec<String>) -> Vec<String>` to keep findings beginning with that id. Import `spell_def` from `crate::rules::fixtures::catalog` and `put`/`slot` from `crate::rules::fixtures::harness`. Add `i11_unit_tokens_in_graveyard_exile_or_held_are_flagged_and_a_spell_token_in_graveyard_is_allowed`: use `new_instance` with `fx-token-rush` and the corresponding `Zone` to build isolated P1-graveyard and P2-exile states, and construct `HeldCard { holder_id, holder_mark, to, card, exile_on_release: None }` for the held state; assert one location-specific I11 finding in each. Clone `catalog_override()`, insert `spell_def(999, json!({ "token": true, "rarity": "Token" }))`, re-register it, plant `fx-999` in a graveyard, and assert no I11 finding.

7. In the same test file, add `i12_a_non_deft_unit_that_switched_cannot_declare_an_attack_but_deft_can`. Add a local setup helper that starts from `playing`, uses `put`/`slot` to put the chosen definition in P1’s unit lane 1 and `fx-21` in P2’s unit lane 1, and returns the state plus both ids. Call `monitor.before` with `ActionBody::SwitchPosition`, feed `GameEvent::PositionSwitched { position: Position::Def }`, then call `before` with `ActionBody::Attack` and feed `GameEvent::AttackDeclared { forced: false, instead_of: None }`; assert an I12 finding for `fx-1`, and repeat with `cb-deft-duelist` asserting no I12 finding. Filter out unrelated I3/I4 findings from the deliberately planted event stream.

8. Add `i12_a_windfury_unit_that_attacked_once_cannot_switch` beside it, reusing that helper with `cb-windfurier`. Feed one chosen `ActionBody::Attack` and matching non-forced declaration, then one chosen `ActionBody::SwitchPosition` and matching position-switch event in the same turn and stint; assert one I12 finding, proving R636’s first attack consumes the switch exertion even though I2 still permits a second attack.

9. Update only invariant-range prose in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, `crates/tools/src/fused_pairs.rs`, and `crates/tools/README.md`: say I1–I12 run after every applicable action/per duel, identify I11 as the off-field Unit-token scan and I12 as the switch/attack shadow, and preserve the existing statement that only the expensive I6 and I8 checks are sampled by strides.

10. Run the targeted tests and checks below. Then run all three requested 200-seed waves. If a new I11/I12 finding appears, reproduce its exact seed with `--from <seed> --seeds 1` and the same mode, determine whether the engine or oracle is wrong, and do not weaken the invariant. A genuine gameplay bug is outside the listed monitor-only files: report the seed and required owner file for a follow-up rather than silently broadening or suppressing this patch.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` — `i11_unit_tokens_in_graveyard_exile_or_held_are_flagged_and_a_spell_token_in_graveyard_is_allowed`: all three forbidden Unit-token locations fail I11; a Spell token in graveyard passes.
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` — `i12_a_non_deft_unit_that_switched_cannot_declare_an_attack_but_deft_can`: the same stint rejects the non-Deft switch/attack pair and accepts Deft.
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` — `i12_a_windfury_unit_that_attacked_once_cannot_switch`: Windfury’s first declaration spends the shared switch exertion.

Run:

1. `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test rules invariants::i11_unit_tokens_in_graveyard_exile_or_held_are_flagged_and_a_spell_token_in_graveyard_is_allowed`
2. `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test rules invariants::i12_a_non_deft_unit_that_switched_cannot_declare_an_attack_but_deft_can`
3. `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test rules invariants::i12_a_windfury_unit_that_attacked_once_cannot_switch`
4. `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit`
5. `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`
6. `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --all-targets --features testkit -- -D warnings`
7. `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`
8. `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`
9. `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200 --handicap`
10. `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200 --duos`
11. `cargo fmt --check`
12. `cargo jackioh catalog check`
13. `cargo jackioh patches check`
14. `cargo jackioh spec check`

## Done when

- [ ] I11 flags definition-level Unit tokens in both players’ graveyard/exile piles and in `state.held`, while a Spell token in graveyard is clean.
- [ ] I12 flags switch→attack and attack→switch for one non-Deft turn/stint, including Windfury after attack one, while Deft’s independent halves pass.
- [ ] Effect-driven switches, forced attacks, re-entry, and a confirmed kill-credit refresh do not create false positives.
- [ ] The same `InvariantMonitor::after` checks run for both Duos duels and the docs consistently say I1–I12.
- [ ] The three named engine regression tests, engine testkit tests, tools tests, both clippy commands, and all three 200-seed waves pass.
- [ ] Formatting, catalog, patches and spec checks pass, with no generated-file or unrelated diff.

## Risks

- The monitor is an independent oracle: reading `exertion.switched` or calling `combat::has_exertion` would duplicate the implementation and miss a shared bug. Use only chosen actions, events, turn/stint shadow state, layered Deft, and the existing independently-settled kill-credit shadow.
- `positionSwitched` is also emitted by effects. Requiring the pending chosen switch prevents R20 false positives; consuming/resetting that pending marker prevents stale matches in Duos’ other duel.
- A Unit may die during its attack, so the pre-reduction Deft/identity snapshot must supply the message and keyword decision when `find_instance` no longer can. Keep iteration and messages deterministic so fuzz signatures and seed reproduction remain stable.
- Do not add a ruling: §3/§3.2/§4.1 and R11/R49/R636 already settle every behavior here.

## Open questions

None.
```
